summary: David Ralph Quinter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his MA at the University of Colorado Boulder and his PhD at Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, becoming associate professor of East Asian religions at the University of Alberta (attested 2019).
David Reigle works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held a post at Asian Humanities Press (attested 2006).

David Roy Shackleton Bailey was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge (Litt.D. 1958), he held posts at Cambridge, Harvard University (1975–1988), and the University of Michigan (1968; 1988–2002).
David Ruddell was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Laval University and served as Secretary at Fort William College.

David Schaberg is a Sinologist who studied at Stanford University (~1982–1986) and earned his PhD in Comparative Literature at Harvard (~1989–1996). At UCLA, he joined the Department of Asian Languages and Cultures in 1996, served as dean of Humanities (2012), and became Professor (2020).

David Seyfort Ruegg was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the EPHE (~1952–1957). He held chairs and professorships at Leiden University (1966–1972), the University of Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS University of London (~1985–1996).

David Shea was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological linguist who studied at Trinity College Dublin in 1793. Until 1836, he served as Assistant Professor of Oriental Languages at East India Company College.
David Slakter works in Indology and philosophy. He completed a master's degree at the University of Liverpool in 2012 under the supervision of Christopher Bartley.
David Steindl-Rast is a religious studies scholar who completed his studies at the University of Vienna and the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna.

David Tracy was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University. He taught at the Catholic University of America (1967–1969) and the University of Chicago from 1969 to 2006.

David W. Chappell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale (Ph.D. ~1968–1976), he served as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1972–2002) and later taught at Soka University of America (~2002–2004).

David W. Tien is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisor James Robson.
David Webster is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Peter Harvey.

Davoud Monchi-Zadeh was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and under Walther Wüst, later holding posts at the University of Munich (~1943–1945), Alexandria University (~1951–1952), and Uppsala University (~1953–1979).
Daw Ohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied at the University of Rangoon and served there as Tutor in Pali (attested 1977).

Dawa Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and history who studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi, and UC Berkeley (MA, PhD 1976–1982). He served as Professor of Central Asian Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1986–2004).
Dawa Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle and at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. He has held a post at Tibet University.

Daya Krishna was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served as professor of philosophy and Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1969–1984) and as chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (~1991–1994).

Daya Ram Sahni was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Oriental College and the University of the Punjab. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (1925–1935) and later directed archaeology in Jaipur State and Jammu and Kashmir.

Dayananda Saraswati was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Sri Jayachamarajendra Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya and under teachers including Virajanand Dandeesha (~1860–1863), P. S. Subramania Iyer, Swami Pranavananda, and Swami Tapovan Maharaj.
